confidence_notes: I based the food and coffee prices on one web search of cost-of-living sites (CityCost, updated Oct 2026; Nomadranker; MyLifeElsewhere). Those sites gave a cappuccino at about $4-5.40, a cheap meal at $5-9 and a mid-range meal for two at $17-39. I picked values toward the upper-middle of those ranges. Beer is costly in Muscat: alcohol is heavily taxed and mostly served in hotel bars and licensed restaurants. One source put it at about $13, and hotel bars at $13-18. I found no direct price for cocktails or wine. I estimated them from the local beer price and typical Gulf hotel-bar pricing, so they are less certain. The accommodation prices are my own estimates from general knowledge. I didn't check any booking sites. Muscat has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel prices are especially uncertain. July is the hot low season, which tends to push hotel prices down.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Muscat with other Gulf cities that have licensed alcohol, such as Doha, Manama and Abu Dhabi. Muscat's food prices are a little lower than those cities, but its alcohol prices are similar.
